title: Robert Taylor's Nehi Revue show in 1927
summary: He joined trumpeter Robert Taylor's Nehi Revue with chorus girls and comedians, played New Orleans theaters and toured to Michigan and Seattle before leaving for Miss Broadway.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: From then on, what happened then, I got with a trumpet player called Robert Taylor. He's originally from New Orleans and he was a show man. I don't know anything about it. He had a show you called Taylor's Nehi Revue Show. That was in 1927. He had a show you called Robert Taylor's Nehi Revue Show. All right. So I got with his show. And we used to show at the Coliseum Theater, show around and down. We showed at the Lincoln Theater when the Lincoln Theater was on Louisiana

Avenue where Frank Goodwin Hospital is. Oh, I didn't even know what it was up there. Lincoln Theater used to be there. Right where Frank Goodwin Hospital is. It's still over now on Washington Street. It's called Lincoln now, isn't it?

Well, it used to be on ... That where there's Hospitals. In fact, it used to be on Howard and Louisiana Avenue. Yeah. See, at that time, it wasn't on the South Street. It was Howard Street. There's still a lot of people ... Well, at that time, Robert Taylor's Nehi Revue Show, that's where we used to do all our rehearsing. And he was a trumpet player. He was. And he was a good trumpet player. But he was mostly a show man. Yeah. He had his own show. When I worked with Taylor, I ...
They have dancers and all there? Oh, yeah. He had a whole front line of chorus girls.

Yeah. He had 10 chorus girls. Yeah. And four comedians. Comedians, yeah. Yeah. Had a big show. Well, I traveled around with him. I expected ... Well, I went all through Michigan. I would say from here all through the states on into Michigan. Yeah. I went through Seattle, Washington with him. I worked around back in my younger days. Then what happened? I worked back to Dallas, Texas with him. I quit him to get with a show out of Chicago called Billy Pearson Show. The man's name was Billy Pearson. The man of the show, but the original, the name of the show was Miss Broadway. Yeah. Well, I was supposed to be a pretty good show drummer then. I was learning more and more. Well, and everywhere I would go and play shows in the different theaters and different showmen would see me play shows. They wanted me to join them and always offer me a little more money. So I got with Billy Pearson, which is Miss Broadway's show. And I played around with him.
